Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:10:1.hebrew: מתחילתו משמט - מתחילת השנה, מיו"כ, עבדים נפטרים ושדות חוזרות, ועדיין לא עברו אלא מ"ט. אבל שביעית אינה משמטת אלא בסופה, דכתיב (דברים טו) מקץ שבע שנים — לסוף שבע שנים, כל שנה שביעית במנין — ס"א:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:10:1.english: From its beginning it releases - From the beginning of the year, from Yom Kippur, slaves are released and fields return [to their owners], and only forty-nine [years] have yet passed. But the Sabbatical [Year] releases only at its end, as it is written: “At the end of seven years” (Deuteronomy 15:1) — at the end of seven years, [meaning] every seventh year in the count — [a variant reading in] other books.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:11:1.hebrew: תחילת דינו - ליום הדין, תחילת תביעות שעליו — מפני מה לא עסקת בתורה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:11:1.english: The beginning of his judgment - On the Day of Judgment, the first of the claims against him [is]: "Why did you not engage in Torah?"

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:11:2.hebrew: פוטר מים - הפורק עול תורה. ״ראשית מדון״ — הוא תחילת דינו. ואין מים אלא תורה, דכתיב (ישעיהו נ״ה:א׳): ״הוי כל צמא לכו למים״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:11:2.english: He who lets out water - [This refers to] one who casts off the yoke of Torah. “The beginning of strife” — that is the beginning of his judgment. And “water” is nothing other than Torah, as it is written (Isaiah 55:1): “Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the water.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:12:1.hebrew: וכשם שדין - פורענות תורה קודם לדין פורענות מעשה, כך שכרו — אם עסק בתורה — קודם לשכר מעשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:12:1.english: And just as the judgment - [Of] retribution for [neglecting] Torah precedes the judgment of retribution for action, so too its reward — if one engaged in Torah — precedes the reward for action.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:12:2.hebrew: בעבור ישמרו חוקיו - ואמר מר לעיל (קידושין דף לז.): ״תשמרון״ — זו משנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:12:2.english: That they might observe His statutes - And the Master said above (Kiddushin 37a): “That you shall observe” — this is Mishnah [study].

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:12:3.english: They will protect - They will fulfill [them].

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:13:1.hebrew: ופסול לעדות - דכיון שאינו מן היישוב, אין מקפיד על עצמו ואין לו בושת פנים. וכן האוכל בשוק, הואיל ואין מקפיד על כבודו, אינו בוש לזלזל בעצמו וליפסל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:13:1.english: And [he is] disqualified from bearing witness - For since he is not part of civilized society, he is not particular about himself and has no sense of shame. And similarly, one who eats in the marketplace — since he is not particular about his dignity, he is not ashamed to degrade himself and be disqualified.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:2:1.hebrew: לפי שהעולם נידון אחר רובו כו' - יראה אדם עצמו כאילו שקול, כל העולם שקול — כמחצה צדיקים וחסידים ומחצה רשעים — וכאילו מעשיו שקולים כמחצה על מחצה. עשה מצוה אחת — נמצאו זכיותיו מכריעין, ונמצא צדיק, ועל ידו כל העולם הוכרע להיות רובן צדיקים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:2:1.english: Since the world is judged by its majority, etc. - A person should view himself as though [he is] balanced, [and] the entire world [as] balanced — about half righteous and pious [people] and half wicked [people] — and as though his [own] deeds are balanced half-and-half. [If] he performs one mitzvah, his merits are found to tip the balance, and he is found [to be] righteous, and through him the entire world is tipped so that its majority is righteous.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:4:1.hebrew: וניהוי - צדיק שמרד כמחצה עונות וכמחצה זכיות, ולמה איבד את הראשונות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:4:1.english: And let him be - A righteous person who rebelled [should be considered] as [one with] half sins and half merits, and why did he lose the earlier [merits]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:4:2.english: In [the case of one who] regrets - He regrets all the good [deeds] that he did.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:6:1.english: To what are the righteous compared in this world - With respect to the afflictions that come upon them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:6:2.english: And its branches - That is to say, a small part of it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:6:3.english: [If] it is cut - Its branch [is cut off] from it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:6:4.hebrew: כך - נפרעין מן הצדיקים מעט עונות שבידם, ונמצאו כולם נקיים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:6:4.english: So too - Retribution is exacted from the righteous for the few sins that are in their hand, and they are all found [to be] pure.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:7:1.english: And to what are the wicked in this world compared? - In the good that is bestowed upon them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:7:2.hebrew: נופו - מעט ממנו. אף אלו יש בידם מיעוט טובות וזכיות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:7:2.english: Its branches - A small part of it. So too, these [wicked] possess a minority of good deeds and merits.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:7:3.english: Its branches are cut off - The receipt of their reward is the cutting off of their branches.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:7:4.hebrew: למדרגה - אשולויי"א (אישילייר"א: מדרגה), כדרך שעושין מדרגות לחריצין שסביבות המגדלים, כשמגביהי' קרקעיתן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:7:4.english: To the step - [In Old French,] escheloire (esjaliere: a step) — in the manner that they make steps for the trenches that surround towers when they raise their bottom.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:7:5.hebrew: יש דרך ישר לפני איש - כשרואין הרשעים שלותן, נראית דרכם בעיניהם ישרה, ואחריתה של אותה שלוה — הזמנת דרכי מות היתה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:7:5.english: There is a way which seems right to a man - When the wicked see their prosperity, their way appears right in their eyes, and the end of that prosperity was the preparation for the ways of death.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:8:1.english: The house of Nit’za - [Nit’za is] the name of the man.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:8:2.english: For study leads to action - Both are found in his hand.

Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:9:1.hebrew: גדול תלמוד תורה שקדם לחלה ארבעים שנה - כשיצאו ממצרים נתנה להם תורה בחדש השלישי, ובחלה לא נתחייבו עד שנכנסו לארץ, דכתיב: "בבאכם". ואמר מר (ספרי פ' שלח לך): משונה ביאה זו מכל ביאות שבתורה, דכתיב בהו "כי תבאו", וכאן נאמר "בבאכם" — משנכנסו לה. ובתרומות ומעשרות — לאחר כיבוש וחילוק, דכתיב: "תבואת זרעך", שיהא כל אחד מכיר חלקו, והן י"ד שנים — הרי נ"ד. ומשם התחילו למנות שמיטין, כדאמרינן בערכין (דף יב:), ועשו שמיטה לסוף שבע — הרי ס"א שנים, ולסוף נ' עשו יובל — הרי ק"ג:
Rashi on Kiddushin 40b:9:1.english: Torah study is greater, as it preceded ḥalla by forty years - When they went out of Egypt, the Torah was given to them in the third month. And for ḥalla, they did not become obligated until they entered the Land, as it is written: “When you come” (Numbers 15:18). And the Master said (Sifrei, Parashat Shelaḥ Lekha): This entry is different from all other entries in the Torah, as in them it is written: “When you enter,” whereas here it is stated: “When you come” — [meaning,] as soon as they entered it. And for terumot and tithes, [they became obligated only] after conquest and division, as it is written: “[all] the yield of your seed” (Deuteronomy 14:22) — that each one should recognize his portion; and these [years of conquest and division] were fourteen years — behold, fifty-four [years]. And from there they began to count Sabbatical [cycles], as we say in Arakhin (12b), and they observed a Sabbatical year at the end of seven [years] — behold, sixty-one years; and at the end of fifty [years] they observed a Jubilee — behold, 103 [years].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 40b:11:1.hebrew: אין תחילת דינו של אדם אלא על דברי תורה - והא דאמר בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת לא.): "כשמכניסין אדם לדין אומרים לו: נשאת ונתת באמונה?" — היינו דווקא לענין שאלה ששואלין לו על משא ומתן; אבל מ"מ נפרעים ממנו תחלה על שלא קבע עתים לתורה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 40b:11:1.english: "The beginning of a person’s judgment is only concerning matters of Torah" - And that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 31a): "When a person is brought in for judgment, they say to him: 'Did you conduct business faithfully?'" — that is specifically with regard to the questioning, that they ask him about business transactions [first]; but nevertheless, punishment is exacted from him first for not having set fixed times for Torah [study].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 40b:13:1.hebrew: ויש אומרים אף פסול לעדות - פירש בקונטרס: הואיל ואינו מקפיד על עצמו, אינו בוש לזלזל בעצמו ולפסול. וקשה: אמאי פסול לעדות הוא? הא אמרינן בירושלמי: ר"ש ברבי הוה אכיל בשוקא, חזיה ר"מ, אמר לו: "אין שבח לתלמיד לאכול בשוק" — משמע דלאחר אין קפידא! ופי' ר"ח, דהכא מיירי שחוטף ואוכל. וא"ת: אם כן, פשיטא דפסול, דגזלן הוא! וי"ל, שחוטף פחות משוה פרוטה; אי נמי, שגזל דבר שאינו מקפיד עליו. והר"ר אליהו מפרש, כגון שהלך אצל המוכרים וטועם משל כולם מעט מעט, כאילו רוצה לקנות מהם. וניחא השתא שקורין "כלב" — שדומה לכלב: אוכל כאן מעט וכאן מעט. ור"ת פירש, דאוכל בשוק היינו שאוכל סעודה דפת, דגנאי יותר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 40b:13:1.english: "And some say [he is] even disqualified from bearing witness" - Rashi explained: Since he is not particular about himself, he is not ashamed to degrade himself and become disqualified. And it is difficult: Why is he disqualified from bearing witness? Behold, we say in the Yerushalmi: Rabbi Shimon bar Rebbi was eating in the marketplace; Rabbi Meir saw him [and] said to him: "It is not praiseworthy for a disciple [of the Sages] to eat in the marketplace" — which implies that for another [person], there is no objection! And Rabbeinu Chananel explained that here [the baraita] is dealing with [one] who snatches and eats. And if you say: If so, it is obvious that he is disqualified, for he is a robber! And one can say: That he snatches [an amount worth] less than the value of a perutah; alternatively, that he took something about which [the owner] is not particular. And the Rabbi, Rabbi Eliyahu explains: For example, where he went to the merchants and tastes a little bit from each of them, as if he wants to buy from them. And it is well understood now why they call [him] "a dog" — for he is similar to a dog: eating a little here and a little there. And Rabbeinu Tam explained that "one who eats in the marketplace" means that he eats a meal of bread, which is more disgraceful.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 40b:8:1.hebrew: תלמוד גדול שהתלמוד מביא לידי מעשה - תימה, דאמר בספ"ק דב"ק (דף יז.): ר' יוחנן משי ידיה ומנח תפילין, והדר אמר לן: "קיים" אמרינן, "לימד" לא אמרי'. ופריך: והא אמר מר: גדול תלמוד תורה שהתלמוד מביא לידי מעשה? פירש בקונטרס: מי נתלה במי? קטן נתלה בגדול. וא"כ, כיון דאמר "קיים", כל שכן "לימד", שאינו חשוב כל כך! אלמא מוכח התם מהכא דמעשה גדול. וי"ל, דהתם הכי פי': "והדר אמר לן: קיים אמרינן, לימד לא אמרינן"; ופריך התם: והאמר מר גדול תלמוד שמביא לידי מעשה? א"כ, היאך קיים אם לא לימד? וכיון שאנו אומרים לו "קיים", הרי אומרים לו "לימד", ואת אמרת "קיים" אמרינן, "לימד" לא אמרי'! ומשני: הא למיגמר, הא לאגמורי. כלומר: למגמר לדידיה ודאי מעשה עדיף, אבל לאגמורי אחרינא ודאי עדיף טפי ממעשה, והלכך "לימד" לאחריני לא אמרי'. וי"מ, דאדם שלא למד עדיין ובא לימלך אם ילמוד תחילה או יעסוק במעשה — אומרים לו: למוד תחלה, לפי שאין עם הארץ חסיד; אבל אדם שלמד כבר — המעשה טוב יותר מלימוד:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 40b:8:1.english: Study is greater, for study leads to action - [This is] astonishing, for [the Gemara] says at the end of the first chapter of Bava Kamma (17a): Rabbi Yoḥanan washed his hands, donned phylacteries, and then said to us: [Regarding a deceased scholar,] we say "he fulfilled," [but] we do not say "he taught." And [the Gemara there] objects: But didn't the Master say: Torah study is great because study leads to action? Rashi explained: Which is dependent on which? The lesser is dependent on the greater. And if so, since he said [that we say] "he fulfilled," all the more so [should we say] "he taught," which is not as significant! Thus, it is proved there from here that action is greater. And one can say that there, this is the explanation: "And then he said to us: We say 'he fulfilled,' [but] we do not say 'he taught'"; and [the Gemara] objects there: But didn't the Master say: Study is great because it leads to action? If so, how did he fulfill if he did not learn? And since we say about him "he fulfilled," we are effectively saying about him "he taught," yet you said: We say "he fulfilled," [but] we do not say "he taught"! And [the Gemara] resolves: This [statement] is for learning [for oneself], and that [statement] is for teaching [others]. That is to say: To learn for oneself, action is certainly superior; but to teach others is certainly far superior to action, and therefore "he taught" to others we do not say. And some explain: [As for] a person who has not yet learned and comes to consult whether he should learn first or engage in action, we tell him: "Learn first," because an ignoramus cannot be pious; but for a person who has already learned, action is better than study.
